newsitem.title: FRANCE: MEP Hughes lashes Britain over working time directive.
newsitem.headline: MEP Hughes lashes Britain over working time directive.

text.p: Stephen Hughes, a British Labour Member of the European Parliament, accused the British government on Tuesday of engaging in wrecking tactics and wasting taxpayers' money over the working time directive.

After the European Court of Justice threw out all but one of Britain's arguments the Chairman of the Social Affairs Committee said Britain should now quickly apply the directive, but would not and the Commission would probably end up taking London to court after the forthcoming General Election.
"The Commission will probably sit and wait because there is a general election coming up. I think the IGC will effectively be suspended until after the British election," he told Reuters.
He said that on the one hand it had said it would consult over implementation but on the other push for a repeal of the directive under the IGC.

He said that the one part of the Court judgment which went in Britain's favour -- deletion of the clause which says that the minimum period of rest should in principle include Sunday -- would annoy a lot of people.
"The only piece of the judgment which...will go in the British favour will annoy a lot of people," he said.

Hughes said a repeal of the directive would be impossible because it would entail abolishing a whole range of EU health and safety legislation under Article 118a of the EU treaty, which member states are already implementing.

Hughes said the British government had shot itself in the foot because the Court had ruled that the correct definition of health and safety was the Danish one, which includes psychological well-being, including stress, which is wider in scope than the definition most people had been using so far.
